title: Indian Economy — Basic Concepts & Five-Year Plans
shortDescription: Economic jargon looks scary until you translate it into plain language — GDP, fiscal policy, and the Five-Year Plan numbering are mostly just vocabulary.
genZNote: Economic jargon looks scary until you translate it into normal human language. GDP is just 'everything the country made, add it up'.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: Static-GK Economy questions mostly test DEFINITIONS (what GDP/GNP/fiscal deficit mean), INSTITUTIONS (RBI, NITI Aayog, and their roles), and the Five-Year Plan sequence/numbering — not live statistics, which change constantly and belong to Current Affairs instead.

rows: Total value of all goods and services produced WITHIN a country's borders in a period, regardless of who produced them
GDP plus net income earned by the country's residents from abroad, minus income earned by foreigners domestically
The gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding borrowings), in a given year
Levied directly on income/wealth of the payer, e.g. income tax — cannot be shifted to someone else
Levied on goods/services, e.g. GST — can be passed on from seller to buyer
A general, sustained rise in the price level of goods and services over time

sections.heading: Five-Year Plans — the Sequence
sections.body: India's Five-Year Plans were formulated by the Planning Commission, starting with the First Five-Year Plan (1951–56). The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in January 2015, after which the Five-Year Plan system was discontinued in favour of other planning approaches.
bullets: First Five-Year Plan (1951–56): focused on agriculture and irrigation, including major dam projects.
The Planning Commission (est. 1950) drafted and oversaw the Five-Year Plans until its replacement.
NITI Aayog (2015) replaced the Planning Commission with a more advisory, cooperative-federalism-oriented role rather than the older centralised planning model.

sections.heading: Key Economic Institutions
bullets: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) — India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance, and regulating the banking system.
NITI Aayog — policy think tank/advisory body that replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) — regulates the securities/stock markets.
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) — audits government accounts and expenditure (a constitutional body, also covered under the Constitution's constitutional bodies).

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Confusing GDP (produced within the country's borders) with GNP (includes residents' income from abroad) — the distinction is about WHO earned it and WHERE, not just a synonym pair.
Assuming direct and indirect taxes can be told apart by amount or importance — the real distinction is whether the tax burden can be shifted to someone else (indirect) or not (direct).
Treating NITI Aayog as simply a renamed Planning Commission with the same powers — it has a distinctly more advisory, less centrally-directive role.

sections.heading: Fast Recall Hooks
bullets: First Five-Year Plan: 1951–56, agriculture and irrigation focus.
Planning Commission (1950) → NITI Aayog (Jan 2015) — note the year of the switch.
GDP = produced within borders. GNP = GDP + net income from abroad.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Indian Economy static GK covers core definitions (GDP, GNP, fiscal deficit, direct/indirect tax), the Five-Year Plan sequence, and key institutions like the RBI and NITI Aayog.
keyFacts: GDP: value of goods/services produced within the country. GNP: GDP + net income from abroad.
First Five-Year Plan: 1951–56, focused on agriculture and irrigation.
Planning Commission (1950) was replaced by NITI Aayog in January 2015.
Direct tax cannot be shifted to another party; indirect tax can be passed on (e.g. GST).
commonConfusion: GDP and GNP are not synonyms — GNP adds net income earned abroad by residents and subtracts income earned domestically by foreigners.

highYieldFacts: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in January 2015, ending the Five-Year Plan system.
First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture and irrigation.
commonTraps: Treating GDP and GNP as interchangeable terms.
Assuming NITI Aayog has the same centralised planning powers as the old Planning Commission.
mustRemember: Direct tax = on the payer's own income/wealth, non-transferable. Indirect tax = on goods/services, transferable (e.g. GST).
